g|present-continuous|1i2skmr.sig: Listen! Someone ___ (knock) at the door.#is knocking#knocks/knock/knocking
ex: Look! The cat *is climbing* the tree.

en.why: ‘Listen!’ signals an action happening at this moment, requiring present continuous.

wrong.knocks: Simple present, not an immediate action.
wrong.knock: Missing auxiliary *is*; not a complete progressive form.
wrong.knocking: Missing auxiliary *is*; not a complete progressive form.

g|present-simple|1aa0ovf.sig: My father ___ (watch) the news every evening.#watches#watch/watchs/is watch

en.why: Third‑person singular verbs ending in –ch add –es.

wrong.is watch: Uses *is* + base verb, not present simple.

g|present-simple|1pa6au1.sig: Phần nào sai? My brother (A) doesn't (B) likes (C) travelling by plane because he (D) gets anxious.#(B) likes#(A) doesn't/(C) travelling/(D) gets

en.why: After the auxiliary *doesn't*, the main verb must be in base form.
en.hook: doesn't + like = base verb, not likes

wrong.(A) doesn't: ‘doesn't’ is correct; it isn’t the error.
wrong.(D) gets: ‘gets’ is correct for the second clause.

g|present-simple|1qtnrqq.sig: Task 1 (quy trình): Once the grapes are harvested, the juice ___ into large steel tanks.#is poured#was poured/is pouring/has poured
ex: The mixture *is mixed* in a bowl.

en.why: Use present simple passive to describe a routine process.

wrong.was poured: Past tense, not suitable for a regular process.
wrong.is pouring: Active progressive, changes meaning to ongoing action.
wrong.has poured: Present perfect active, not a passive description.

en.why: *Does* is the correct auxiliary for a third‑person singular subject in present‑simple questions.

wrong.Do: Used with plural subjects, not *your university*.
wrong.Is: Not an auxiliary for the verb *offer*.
wrong.Has: Changes the tense; not used for simple present questions.

g|present-simple|2px7jf.sig: Public transport in my city ___ (be) quite cheap.#is#are/be/being

en.why: Singular uncountable noun takes singular verb *is* in present simple.

wrong.are: Plural verb, not used with singular noun.
wrong.be: Infinitive form, cannot serve as main verb here.
wrong.being: Present participle, not a finite verb in this clause.

g|present-simple|5a12p2.sig: Phần nào sai? Each of the participants (A) receive a certificate (B) when the course (C) finishes (D) at the end of June.#(A) receive#(B) when/(C) finishes/(D) at the end of
ex: Each of the students *receives* a badge.
Each of the books *lies* on the shelf.

en.why: ‘Each of’ makes the subject singular, so the verb takes –s.

wrong.(B) when: ‘when’ would start a time clause, not a verb error.
wrong.(C) finishes: ‘finishes’ is correct for ‘the course’, not the highlighted mistake.
wrong.(D) at the end of: The phrase is fine; it isn’t the error.

g|present-simple|p009x7.sig: The flight to Singapore ___ at 6 a.m. tomorrow, according to the timetable.#departs#is departing to/depart/departed

en.why: Timetabled future events use simple present; third‑person singular adds –s.

wrong.is departing to: Unnecessary *to* and progressive form; not used with timetables.
wrong.departed: Past tense; the schedule refers to the future.

g|present-simple|pjgd9q.sig: Câu nào đúng ngữ pháp?#Does she speak French fluently?#Does she speaks French fluently?/Do she speak French fluently?/She speak French fluently?

en.why: Form a question with *does* + subject + base verb; no –s added.

wrong.Do she speak French fluently?: Wrong auxiliary; *do* is not used with *she*.
